title: Middle East Travel Guide
summary: A balanced Middle East travel guide highlighting modern cities, desert adventures, cultural etiquette, and practical planning for first-time visitors.
bestTime: October–April for cooler days in the Gulf and pleasant desert weather across the region.

quickFacts.Language: Arabic is primary; English is widely used in tourism.
quickFacts.Visa: E-visas available for many countries; some require advance approval.
quickFacts.Dress Code: Modest clothing recommended in public and around religious sites.

attractions.name: Dubai
attractions.summary: Futuristic skyscrapers, luxury malls, desert safaris, and vibrant nightlife.

attractions.name: Abu Dhabi
attractions.summary: Cultural landmarks like Sheikh Zayed Mosque and luxury cultural districts.

attractions.name: Petra
attractions.summary: Ancient rock-cut city in Jordan and one of the world’s most iconic archaeological wonders.

attractions.name: Muscat
attractions.summary: A quieter Gulf experience with old souks, forts, and scenic coastal landscapes.

attractions.name: Dead Sea
attractions.summary: The lowest point on Earth, famous for buoyant salt water and healing mud.

cultureEtiquette: Dress respectfully in public, especially near mosques and cultural sites.
Avoid public displays of affection in conservative areas.
Accept hospitality politely and avoid criticizing local religion or politics.
gettingAround: Use ride-hailing apps in major cities for safe and convenient travel.
Take domestic airlines for longer Gulf journeys between the UAE, Oman, and Jordan.
Book guided tours for desert safaris and heritage site visits.
sustainability: Choose eco-friendly tours and avoid plastic bottles in the desert.
Respect dune preservation rules during desert safaris.
Support local businesses and cultural artisans when shopping.

faqs.q: Is the Middle East safe for tourists?
faqs.a: Major tourist destinations are generally safe, but always follow local travel advisories and respect local customs.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa for the UAE?
faqs.a: Many nationalities can obtain an e-visa or visa on arrival; check the latest UAE rules before travel.
Pack modest clothing for cultural sites and lightweight layers for desert days.
